sentences.en: January of 2020 marked the New York Public Library's 125th anniversary.
sentences.zh: 2020年1月，纽约公共图书馆迎来了125周年纪念。

sentences.en: And to celebrate, they published a list of the 10 most checked out books in the history of the library.
sentences.zh: 为了庆祝，他们公布了一份图书馆史上借阅次数最多的10本书的名单。

sentences.en: And there's one thing about the list that you really can't help but notice right away.
sentences.zh: 这份名单有一点非常引人注目，你一眼就能看出来。
那是我们的制作人，乔·罗森伯格。

sentences.en: It's made up almost entirely of children's books.
sentences.zh: 这份名单几乎全都是儿童读物。

sentences.en: So The Snowy Day, The Cat in the Hat, Where the Wild Things Are, Charlotte's Web.
sentences.zh: 比如《下雪天》、《戴帽子的猫》、《野兽家园》、《夏洛的网》。

sentences.en: Dan Kois is a writer at Slate.
sentences.zh: 丹·科伊斯是《Slate》杂志的一名撰稿人。

sentences.en: To Kill a Mockingbird, arguably a children's book, also on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 《杀死一只知更鸟》——可以说也是一本儿童读物——也在名单上。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, like I read it as a kid.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我小时候读过它。

sentences.en: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone, The Very Hungry Caterpillar.
sentences.zh: 《哈利·波特与魔法石》、《好饿的毛毛虫》。

sentences.en: The only books, quote unquote, for adults on this list are 1984, Fahrenheit 451, and How to Win Friends and Influence People by Dale Carnegie.
sentences.zh: 名单上仅有的几本所谓的“成人书籍”是《1984》、《华氏451》以及戴尔·卡内基的《人性的弱点》。

sentences.en: Love that that book is still on there.
sentences.zh: 很高兴这本书还在名单上。

sentences.en: All told, seven of the 10 books were for kids.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，这10本书中有7本是给孩子看的。

sentences.en: Taken together, they were checked out over two and a half million times.
sentences.zh: 加在一起，它们的借阅次数超过了250万次。

sentences.en: But at the very bottom of the list, Dan Kois noticed this little footnote.
sentences.zh: 但在名单的最底部，丹·科伊斯注意到了这个小注脚。

sentences.en: And it just said, you know, fun fact, Goodnight Moon, of course, one of the most beloved children's books of all time, was not on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 上面写着，你知道，一个有趣的事实：《晚安，月亮》——当然，这是有史以来最受喜爱的儿童读物之一——并没有出现在名单上。

sentences.en: The footnote was almost like an apology.
sentences.zh: 这个注脚几乎像是一种道歉。

sentences.en: Because if there's one title that you'd expect to be on the list, it's Goodnight Moon.
sentences.zh: 因为如果有一本书是你期望出现在名单上的，那一定是《晚安，月亮》。

sentences.en: The famous picture book where the little toddler rabbit says goodnight to all the objects in its massive bedroom.
sentences.zh: 那本著名的绘本，书里的小兔子对着它那巨大卧室里的所有物体说晚安。

sentences.en: Goodnight Socks, Goodnight Clocks, Goodnight, you know, Moon.
sentences.zh: 晚安袜子，晚安时钟，晚安，你知道的，月亮。

sentences.en: I was really surprised, not only because I know of its popularity,
sentences.zh: 我真的很惊讶，不仅因为我知道它很受欢迎，

sentences.en: but because I have always sort of viewed it as a kind of platonically perfect children's picture book for the exact moment in the day when you most need a picture book.
sentences.zh: 还因为我一直把它视为一种柏拉图式的完美儿童绘本，特别适合在一天中你最需要绘本的那个时刻阅读。

sentences.en: That moment when you need your child to fall asleep.
sentences.zh: 就是你需要孩子入睡的那个时刻。

sentences.en: So you can finally take a shower or watch TV or do anything except parent.
sentences.zh: 这样你终于可以去洗个澡、看会儿电视，或者做点除了带孩子以外的任何事。

sentences.en: Still, the book had only been checked out about half as many times as the lowest ranking book on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，这本书的借阅次数只有名单上排名最低的那本书的一半左右。

sentences.en: But it wasn't because of lack of intereSt.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是因为缺乏兴趣。

sentences.en: No, it was because of one person.
According to the New York Public Library, an influential children's librarian at the library had disliked the story so much when it was published in 1947
sentences.zh: 据纽约公共图书馆称，一位有影响力的儿童图书管理员在1947年该书出版时非常讨厌这个故事，

sentences.en: that the library didn't even carry the book until 1972.
sentences.zh: 以至于图书馆直到1972年才引进这本书。

sentences.en: And this librarian's name, according to the press release, was Anne Carroll Moore.
sentences.zh: 根据新闻稿，这位图书管理员的名字叫安妮·卡罗尔·摩尔。

sentences.en: Anne Carroll Moore was the head children's librarian at the New York Public Library for pretty much the whole first half of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 安妮·卡罗尔·摩尔在20世纪上半叶的大部分时间里，一直担任纽约公共图书馆的首席儿童图书管理员。

sentences.en: And for nearly three decades, she single-handedly kept Good Night Moon out of the entire library system.
sentences.zh: 近三十年来，她凭一己之力将《晚安，月亮》挡在了整个图书馆系统之外。

sentences.en: That a children's librarian could just say, no New York Public Library will stock this book.
sentences.zh: 一个儿童图书管理员竟然可以说，纽约公共图书馆不准收藏这本书。

sentences.en: And the idea of, like, children everywhere in the world growing to love Good Night Moon,
sentences.zh: 而且想到全世界的孩子们都逐渐爱上了《晚安，月亮》，

sentences.en: except for in New York City where they grew up sad and Good Night Moon-less, just seemed bananas to me.
sentences.zh: 除了纽约市的孩子们，他们在成长过程中既悲伤又没有《晚安，月亮》陪伴，这对我来说简直太荒谬了。

sentences.en: Now, at this point, if you're imagining your stereotypical, rule-mongering, moralizing librarian giving you the stink eye,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你脑海中浮现出那种刻板印象中爱立规矩、喜欢说教、给你白眼的图书管理员，

sentences.en: Dan Coy says, you don't need to imagine it.
sentences.zh: 丹·科伊斯说，你不需要想象。

sentences.en: At the time that there were finally photographs of her taken, she was an older lady
sentences.zh: 在终于有人给她拍照的时候，她是一位上了年纪的女士，

sentences.en: who looked like the quintessential bun-in-the-hair, shushing librarian who's a really easy villain.
sentences.zh: 看起来就像那种典型的盘着发髻、喜欢嘘人的图书管理员，是一个非常容易塑造的反派。

sentences.en: But as Dan would find out, Moore was, and remains, a very complicated historical figure.
sentences.zh: 但正如丹后来发现的那样，摩尔过去是，现在依然是一个非常复杂的历史人物。

sentences.en: Because long before she became a villainous banner of books, Anne Carole Moore was a hero of children's literature
sentences.zh: 因为在成为臭名昭著的禁书者很久之前，安妮·卡罗尔·摩尔曾是儿童文学的英雄，

sentences.en: who left the world with one undeniably good thing.
sentences.zh: 她给世界留下了一件无可争议的好事。

sentences.en: She pretty much single-handedly invented the children's library.
sentences.zh: 她几乎凭一己之力发明了儿童图书馆。

sentences.en: Jill Lepore is a professor of history at Harvard and a staff writer for The New Yorker
sentences.zh: 吉尔·莱波雷是哈佛大学的历史学教授，也是《纽约客》的特约撰稿人，

sentences.en: who wrote about Moore for the magazine.
sentences.zh: 她曾为该杂志撰写过关于摩尔的文章。

sentences.en: And she says that perhaps no single person has ever done more to get books into the hands of children.
sentences.zh: 她说，也许没有哪个人比她更致力于让孩子们读到书。

sentences.en: And she did so by creating a place for kids to read.
sentences.zh: 她通过为孩子们创造一个阅读空间做到了这一点。

sentences.en: So when you go into your neighborhood public library and there is a thing called the children's room
sentences.zh: 所以，当你走进你社区的公共图书馆，看到有一个叫“儿童阅览室”的地方，

sentences.en: and they have potted plants there and they have toys and they have a cozy rug and a rocking chair
sentences.zh: 那里有盆栽植物、玩具、舒适的地毯和摇椅，

sentences.en: and they have story hours and they have fun art on the walls, like all that stuff was invented by Anne Carole Moore.
sentences.zh: 还有故事时间，墙上还有有趣的艺术品，所有这些都是安妮·卡罗尔·摩尔发明的。

sentences.en: Today, with all the emphasis we place on instilling kids with a love of reading,
sentences.zh: 今天，随着我们越来越强调培养孩子对阅读的热爱，

sentences.en: it's hard to imagine your local public library without a children's reading room.
sentences.zh: 很难想象没有儿童阅览室的当地公共图书馆会是什么样。

sentences.en: But Lepore says that before Moore came along, children weren't even allowed to enter the one place
sentences.zh: 但莱波雷说，在摩尔出现之前，孩子们甚至不被允许进入那个他们

sentences.en: they would be sure to find a book.
Kids really couldn't go to libraries.
sentences.zh: 孩子们真的不能去图书馆。
图书馆是给成年人用的。

sentences.en: The late 19th century saw some of the first public libraries being built in America.
sentences.zh: 19世纪末，美国开始建造第一批公共图书馆。

sentences.en: This was an age in which there was a surge in support for government-funded, progressive institutions
sentences.zh: 那是一个政府资助的进步机构激增的时代，

sentences.en: intended for the betterment of all.
Or, in the case of libraries, the betterment of everyone except children.
sentences.zh: 或者，就图书馆而言，是造福除儿童以外的所有人。

sentences.en: You had to be, I think, 14 or 16 in most places, and in most places you had to be a boy.
sentences.zh: 我想在大多数地方，你必须年满14或16岁，而且在大多数地方，你还得是个男孩。

sentences.en: And the Brooklyn Public Schools had a policy that children below the third grade
sentences.zh: 布鲁克林公立学校曾有一项政策，规定三年级以下的儿童

sentences.en: do not read well enough to profit from the use of library books.
sentences.zh: 阅读能力不足以从图书馆书籍的使用中获益。

sentences.en: The thinking went that if you were too young to read,
sentences.zh: 当时的观点是，如果你太小而不会阅读，

sentences.en: obviously there would be no need for you to go to the library.
sentences.zh: 显然你根本没必要去图书馆。

sentences.en: What good would that do to you?
And if you were old enough to read but you were still a child,
sentences.zh: 如果你已经到了能阅读的年龄，但仍然是个孩子，

sentences.en: going into a library which was full of trashy romance novels and westerns
sentences.zh: 进入一个满是低俗爱情小说和西部小说的图书馆，

sentences.en: And so certainly there's no reason for you to go to a library either.
sentences.zh: 所以当然，你也没有理由去图书馆。

sentences.en: Jill Lepore says that for the children of the wealthy and middle classes,
sentences.zh: 吉尔·莱波雷说，对于富裕家庭和中产阶级的孩子来说，

sentences.en: who often had their own small book collections at home,
sentences.zh: 他们家里通常有自己的小藏书，

sentences.en: being banned from libraries wasn't really a problem.
sentences.zh: 被禁止进入图书馆并不是什么大问题。

sentences.en: But it left the children of the poor with virtually no access to literature.
sentences.zh: 但这让贫困家庭的孩子几乎无法接触到文学作品。

sentences.en: It's completely bound up with class discrimination, right?
sentences.zh: 这完全与阶级歧视有关，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it's not really until the 1920s that you have a very strict regulation against child labor.
sentences.zh: 因为直到20世纪20年代，才有了非常严格的禁止童工的规定。

sentences.en: So the children of the poor are working.
sentences.zh: 所以贫困家庭的孩子都在工作。

sentences.en: They're not even learning to read.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至没有学习阅读。

sentences.en: But then, at the turn of the century,
Anne Carroll Moore, the crusty old librarian who hated Goodnight Moon,
sentences.zh: 安妮·卡罗尔·摩尔，那个讨厌《晚安，月亮》的古板老图书管理员，

sentences.en: came along and flipped the purpose of the library on its head.
sentences.zh: 出现了，并彻底颠覆了图书馆的宗旨。

sentences.en: So I was very surprised recently to read in an article,
sentences.zh: 最近我读到一篇文章时感到非常惊讶，

sentences.en: someone described her as the quintessential librarian with the bun in her hair
sentences.zh: 有人形容她是那种盘着发髻、
喜欢对孩子们嘘人的典型图书管理员，

sentences.en: when in actual fact, that was exactly what she did not do.
sentences.zh: 而事实上，这恰恰是她没有做的事情。

sentences.en: Jan Pinborough is an editor and children's book author.
sentences.zh: 简·平伯勒是一位编辑和儿童书作家。

sentences.en: And she says that in the 1890s,
Moore was the most vocal and energetic among a small group of young progressive librarians
sentences.zh: 摩尔是一小群年轻的进步图书管理员中最直言不讳、最有活力的一位，

sentences.en: who had begun experimenting with a radical idea.
sentences.zh: 他们开始尝试一个激进的想法。

sentences.en: What if they finally let kids into a library,
sentences.zh: 如果他们终于让孩子们进入图书馆，

sentences.en: stocked an area with children's books,
sentences.zh: 在区域内储备儿童读物，

sentences.en: and then made that area just for kids?
sentences.zh: 然后把那个区域专门留给孩子们，会怎样？

sentences.en: And what she was trying to do,
and this is what's really important,
she was trying to provide a childhood to working class kids.
sentences.zh: 她试图为工人阶级的孩子们提供一个童年。

sentences.en: She was trying to give them all the luxury and leisure
sentences.zh: 她试图给他们提供所有的奢侈和闲暇，

sentences.en: of having a space with books that are made for them to be able to read
sentences.zh: 让他们拥有一个摆满专为他们阅读而设计的书籍的空间，

sentences.en: so that they would have what we would think of now as,
sentences.zh: 这样他们就能拥有我们现在所认为的，

sentences.en: you know, a way to address an achievement gap.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一种解决成就差距的方法。

sentences.en: And she was trying to level that field.
sentences.zh: 她试图创造一个公平的竞争环境。

sentences.en: Moore got the chance to run this experiment on an unrivaled scale.
sentences.zh: 摩尔得到了在一个前所未有的规模上进行这项实验的机会。

sentences.en: The New York Public Library was building its iconic main branch
sentences.zh: 纽约公共图书馆正在建造其标志性的主馆，

sentences.en: at the corner of 42nd Street and 5th Avenue.
sentences.zh: 位于第42街和第五大道的拐角处。

sentences.en: And it would feature a dedicated children's reading room
sentences.zh: 它将设有一个专门的儿童阅览室，

sentences.en: that would be designed, stocked, and run by Moore.
sentences.zh: 由摩尔设计、储备和管理。

sentences.en: And there are just these incredible photographs of that children's room
sentences.zh: 有一些非常不可思议的照片记录了那个儿童阅览室，

sentences.en: The photos depict one of the earliest public spaces designed exclusively for kids.
sentences.zh: 这些照片描绘了最早专为儿童设计的公共空间之一。

sentences.en: Moore started by borrowing the idea of kid-sized tables and chairs from kindergartens.
sentences.zh: 摩尔首先从幼儿园借用了儿童尺寸桌椅的想法。

sentences.en: But she took the concept even further.
sentences.zh: 但她把这个概念推得更远。

sentences.en: She had benches, window seats built at the bottoms of the windows, giant windows,
sentences.zh: 她有长凳，在窗户底部建造了窗座，巨大的窗户，

sentences.en: Like if you were five years old, you could sit in those window seats
sentences.zh: 就像如果你五岁，你可以坐在那些窗座上，

sentences.en: and your feet would touch the floor.
Moore especially wanted to provide poorer kids from the tenements
sentences.zh: 摩尔特别希望为来自廉租房的贫困孩子提供

sentences.en: access to the beauty of the natural world.
So she installed pink floor tiles to catch the light coming through the windows,
sentences.zh: 所以她安装了粉红色的地砖来捕捉透过窗户射进来的光线，

sentences.en: and then filled the room with shell collections, butterflies,
and dozens of bowls of freshly cut flowers.
sentences.zh: 以及几十碗鲜切花填满了房间。

sentences.en: And these children, a lot of them were starved for nature.
sentences.zh: 这些孩子，他们中的许多人非常渴望接触自然。

sentences.en: And they would line up for the chance to look at and smell the flowers
sentences.zh: 当她把花拿进来时，他们会排队等着看花、闻花香。
摩尔撤掉了“保持安静”的标志。

sentences.en: Moore took down the silent signs.
sentences.zh: 图书馆现在成了木偶戏、音乐表演

sentences.en: The library was now a space for puppet shows and musical performances
sentences.zh: 和故事时间的空间，故事用多种语言讲述，

sentences.en: and story hours, featuring stories in multiple languages,
sentences.zh: 这样那些还不会读写英语的移民孩子

sentences.en: so that the children of immigrants who did not yet read or speak English

sentences.zh: 但最重要的是，摩尔在新阅览室的书架上摆满了

sentences.en: But most importantly, Moore filled the shelves of the new reading room
sentences.zh: 数百本，最终是数千本儿童读物，

sentences.en: with hundreds, and eventually thousands, of children's books,
sentences.zh: 不是锁在柜子里或富家孩子的育儿室里，

sentences.en: not locked in a cabinet or in a rich kid's nursery,
sentences.zh: 而是放在开放的地方，供任何孩子拿取、翻阅和阅读。

sentences.en: but out in the open for any child to pick up, leaf through, and read.
sentences.zh: 如果孩子喜欢他们手里那本昂贵的书，

sentences.en: And if a child liked the expensive book they were holding,

sentences.zh: 唯一的要求是他们在厚厚的黑色账本上签下自己的名字，

sentences.en: The only requirement was that they sign their name in a big black ledger,

sentences.zh: 当我在这本书上写下我的名字时，

sentences.en: When I write my name in this book,
sentences.zh: 我承诺会好好爱护我在图书馆和家里使用的书籍，

sentences.en: I promise to take good care of the books I use in the library and at home,
and to obey the rules of the library.
And it was a kind of sanctified moment.
sentences.zh: 这份誓言将借书的过程

sentences.en: The pledge turned the process of checking out a book
sentences.zh: 变成了孩子作为公民的第一次行动。

sentences.en: into a child's first act of citizenship.
sentences.zh: 这个阅览室一夜之间就取得了成功。

sentences.en: The room was an overnight success.
sentences.zh: 这个阅览室一夜之间就取得了成功。

sentences.en: Rich and poor kids alike flocked to the library.
sentences.zh: 无论贫富，孩子们都涌向了图书馆。

sentences.en: And Moore began training librarians to establish new reading rooms
sentences.zh: 摩尔开始培训图书管理员，在纽约各地

sentences.en: throughout New York, including Nella Larson,
sentences.zh: 建立新的阅览室，其中包括内拉·拉森，

sentences.en: the prominent African-American writer who created the first children's room in Harlem.
sentences.zh: 这位杰出的非裔美国作家在哈莱姆区创建了第一个儿童阅览室。

sentences.en: By 1913, just two years after the children's room opened,
sentences.zh: 到1913年，也就是儿童阅览室开放仅两年后，

sentences.en: Moore could boast that one-third of the volumes
sentences.zh: 摩尔就能自豪地说，从该市各分馆

sentences.en: borrowed from the city's branch libraries were children's books.
sentences.zh: 借出的图书中，有三分之一是童书。

sentences.en: And children's rooms were springing up even more quickly in the rest of the country.
sentences.zh: 而儿童阅览室在全国其他地区也如雨后春笋般涌现。

sentences.en: By the end of the 1920s, by one estimate,
there were perhaps as many as 1,500 children's rooms in the U.S.
And her reach was really worldwide.
sentences.zh: 她的影响力确实遍及全球。

sentences.en: And there are places and countries where people would say,
sentences.zh: 有些地方和国家的人会说，

sentences.en: well, if you walk into that library,
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你走进那个图书馆，

sentences.en: you'll realize that that was touched by N.
sentences.zh: 你就会意识到那是安·卡罗尔·摩尔

sentences.en: The spread of Moore's reading room model
